summary: E2E test of PARAS REWARD Careers Phase 1 (public page hero+filters+cards) and Phase 2 (Admin CRUD + Applications). Backend: 27/27 careers endpoint tests PASS. Regression: 47/47 tests PASS (L3 bounded arrays, L4 profile pic offload, mall wishlist hotfix, auth hash consolidation, mall mining formula). Frontend: public /careers renders all data-testids (careers-h1, careers-tagline, careers-h2, careers-audience, view-positions-btn, check-status-btn, all 5 filters, job cards with view-details/apply-now buttons). Fresher filter narrows correctly, no-openings empty state appears on unmatched search, check-status dialog opens and submits. Admin /admin/careers loads after admin login, shows Jobs+Applications tabs, stats bar (Total/New/Reviewed/Shortlisted/Interview/Hired), create-job modal opens and successfully creates a job via POST /public/careers/jobs/create (list grew from 1→2), DELETE cleanup returns 200, Applications tab shows 7 apps with status dropdowns and resume download buttons. NO console errors, NO 4xx/5xx observed on shipped flows.

issues: Loading text 'Loading...' spinner appears on very dark background (near-black) during initial React chunk load — low contrast but only visible for ~1s. Not blocking.

action_items: Spec discrepancy (INFO, not a bug): Problem statement says 'Check Application Status' should accept application_id, but frontend + backend implement email-based lookup (GET /public/careers/check-status?email=...). Backend test suite covers this. Main agent should confirm which UX is intended and update spec/docs accordingly.

Apply flow success UX (INFO): On successful submission the UI shows a toast 'Application submitted!' and a success card, but does NOT surface the returned application_id to the user. If users are expected to later 'Check Status' by application_id, they currently have no way to retrieve it. Consider showing application_id in the success state.
critical_code_review_comments: CareersPage.js catches errors silently in fetchJobs (`catch { /* silent */ }`) — a network failure will show an empty page with no error message and no retry. Consider a toast + retry button.
AdminCareers.js is 596 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold. Consider splitting into JobsTab/ApplicationsTab/JobEditorModal components before adding Phase 4.
Frontend /careers uses email as unique identifier for status check but backend has both email lookup and separate application_id record — pick one canonical UX.
